# Auth commands: sign in, and list, switch, check and remove profiles

## `fptctl auth list`

List the stored profiles.

Each profile shows its site, how it signs in (script, user or session), who it signs in as, and whether it is the default. Secrets are never shown.

```text
fptctl auth list [OPTIONS]
```

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth list
fptctl --format table auth list
```

## `fptctl auth login`

Store credentials for a site as a named profile.

Sign in one way: --script-name (an API script and its key), --login (a user and their password) or --session (a session token). The secret is read from a prompt on a terminal, or from stdin otherwise, and goes to the OS keychain; everything else goes to the config file. With --otp, the 2FA code is used once and only the session it opens is stored. The credentials are checked against the site unless --no-verify is given.

```text
fptctl auth login [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--name TEXT`: Profile name. [default: default]
- `--site TEXT`: Site URL, e.g. https://studio.shotgrid.autodesk.com.
- `--script-name TEXT`: Authenticate as this API script.
- `--login TEXT`: Authenticate as this user.
- `--session`: Authenticate with a session token.
- `--http-proxy TEXT`: Proxy as [user:pass@]host[:port].
- `--ca-certs TEXT`: Path to a CA certificate bundle.
- `--otp TEXT`: One-time 2FA code (with --login). Stores a session, not the password.
- `--no-verify`: Store the profile without contacting the site.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth login --site https://studio.shotgrid.autodesk.com --script-name my_script
fptctl auth login --name me --site https://studio.example.com --login jane --otp 123456
```

## `fptctl auth logout`

Remove a profile and its stored secret.

NAME is the profile to remove; without NAME, the default profile. The secret is deleted from the keychain and the profile from the config file. Prints the removed profile and the new default.

```text
fptctl auth logout [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth logout me
fptctl auth logout
```

## `fptctl auth status`

Check that the current credentials work.

Makes one authenticated request with the credentials this command line resolves to: --profile, the FPTCTL_* variables, FPTCTL_PROFILE or the default profile, in that order. Prints the site, the auth type, the identity and where the credentials came from.

```text
fptctl auth status [OPTIONS]
```

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth status
fptctl --profile me auth status
```

## `fptctl auth token`

Print a session token for the current credentials.

The token can sign in later with FPTCTL_SESSION_TOKEN or `auth login --session`, without a password. Each call opens a new session, so the token is different every time.

```text
fptctl auth token [OPTIONS]
```

Library call: `Shotgun.get_session_token`.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth token
fptctl --profile me auth token
```

## `fptctl auth use`

Make NAME the default profile.

NAME is a profile from `fptctl auth list`. Commands use the default profile unless --profile, the FPTCTL_* credential variables or FPTCTL_PROFILE choose another.

```text
fptctl auth use [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Examples:

```shell
fptctl auth use me
```
